name: Unit Roster
description:
Who is on the board, which side they are on, and which tile they stand on. Every tactics component asks one of those three questions and none of them owned the answer: the turn queue rolls initiative per combatant, the movement range floods out from a unit's tile, and cover is priced between an attacker and a defender. Each was written as though somebody else held the roster, and nobody did.

A unit is an identity with a position, not a position with a name. That is why moving is an event this component hears rather than a field a caller writes: movement.grid_movement_range decides which tiles are legal and announces the move, this records where the unit now is, and the two cannot disagree because only one of them is allowed to answer. The same rule ends a unit -- combat.damage_resolver announces the defeat, and removal is this component reacting to it rather than the resolver reaching across.

Stats live here because they are per unit and consulted by everyone: the queue wants a dexterity to break ties, the range wants a movement allowance, the resolver wants hit points. It is deliberately not a character sheet -- progression.attribute_sheet owns the RPG one -- and deliberately not a party: social.party_formation is about who you bring, this is about who is standing here now.

inputs.name: units
inputs.description: The starting board: id, team, tile x and y, and stats. Required, because a roster with a default is somebody else's battle.

inputs.name: teams
inputs.description: Sides, in the order they are offered a turn when initiative ties all the way down. Two is the genre default; three is a free-for-all.

inputs.name: removeOnDefeat
inputs.description: Whether a defeated unit leaves the board. False keeps the body as an obstacle, which some games use as cover and most do not want.

inputs.name: blockOccupiedTiles
inputs.description: Whether a unit's tile is impassable to others. Off for games where units stack or pass through allies -- but the frontline stops meaning anything.

outputs.name: units
outputs.description: Live roster: id, team, x, y, and stats.

outputs.name: unitAt
outputs.description: The unit standing on a tile, or null.

outputs.name: positionOf
outputs.description: The tile a unit id stands on, or null once it is gone.

outputs.name: aliveByTeam
outputs.description: Survivors per team, which is what a victory condition counts.
